releases.title: Choose your accounts, watch your agents, and send files
releases.summary: Pick a subscription account for each agent, add or sign in to accounts from the phone, browse files and send prompt attachments, and watch an agent’s browser or emulator live. Update the phone app and computer together.

features.title: Choose and manage subscription accounts
features.detail: Pick an account when starting an agent, or let Auto pick the signed-in account with the most room left. Add an account, sign in again, rename it, and move a running conversation to another account from the phone.

features.title: Files and prompt attachments built in
features.detail: Browse the agent’s files and send files with a prompt through muxr’s built-in controls.

features.title: Watch an agent’s browser or emulator
features.detail: Open a live view from the session header when an agent is using a browser or Android emulator, and take control when needed.

features.title: Terminal colours and pane map
features.detail: Tune terminal colours in Settings and open a map of the session’s panes from its header.

features.title: Tasks and usage at a glance
features.detail: Agent rows lead with the task, Spaces shows live agent counts, and each provider’s Usage tab shows token counts and trends.

features.title: A private link to your computer
features.detail: Pair with a computer and relay you or someone you trust operates. Confirm the matching words before approving the encrypted link; no muxr-operated account service or relay is required.

fixes.title: Codex agents open from the herd
fixes.detail: Codex panes reported by Herdr now appear as agents you can open, even when Herdr has not attached conversation metadata.

fixes.title: Codex Voice uses your accounts
fixes.detail: Codex Voice planning uses the subscription accounts configured on the computer.

fixes.title: Healthy links stop saying Connecting
fixes.detail: The phone no longer shows a spurious Connecting state while its link is healthy. Pairing and version mismatches also explain what needs attention.

fixes.title: Claude Code follows your finger
fixes.detail: Terminal scrolling includes the landed drag and fling repairs for Claude Code. A further repair for Latest across terminal kinds is still awaiting merge and is not included.

fixes.title: Clearer errors and desktop controls
fixes.detail: Computer request failures show a useful reason, and the desktop key row includes Alt, Super and the other desktop keys. Screen-sharing approval and capture recovery are steadier.

fixes.title: Correct app icons
fixes.detail: Native and web builds use the corrected muxr icons.

fixes.title: Updated connection and agent libraries
fixes.detail: The computer uses the updated Herdr and link libraries for prompts, reads and waits, and removing a paired device clears its relay subscriptions and preserves the revocation.

verification.title: Desktop engine release prerequisite
verification.detail: npm serves the pinned @desklink/host 0.2.0 and Linux x64 engine package, as checked during preparation. This checks availability, not desktop behaviour on the release candidate.

verification.title: Automated checks on the release candidate
verification.detail: The full suite and signed Android/npm candidate build have not been run for this version during changelog preparation. Earlier checks on individual changes are not acceptance of the combined release.

verification.title: Phone and emulator acceptance
verification.detail: The exact signed candidate has not been installed or accepted on a phone or emulator. The installed phone app’s signer still needs comparison with the candidate before choosing direct APK or Play Internal delivery.

verification.title: iOS acceptance
verification.detail: No iOS simulator, device or store build acceptance is recorded for this version.

knownLimits: The phone app and computer must update together: the computer bundles desklink 0.2, which needs the matching new app. Install the phone candidate first, then update the computer before reconnecting.
Latest / jump to the bottom can still fail across terminal kinds. The further repair has not merged and is not part of this source.
A self-hosted computer and relay are required. Installations from before the private-link cutover must update both products and pair again once.
Computer viewing and control require Linux x64 with glibc 2.36 or newer; Wayland input control needs a one-time permission.

features.title: Every agent leads with its task

features.title: Confirm who you connect to

releases.title: Rename anything, and a steadier terminal and Right now
releases.summary: Rename agents, tabs, panes and spaces from the app, keep the terminal's quick actions while you type, and trust that Right now shows the latest reading.

features.title: Rename agents, tabs, panes and spaces
features.detail: Long-press an agent, tab, pane or space and choose Rename. The new name is saved on your computer, so every device and the desk see it, and automatic naming leaves it alone. If a name cannot be used, the app says why.

fixes.title: Right now stays current
fixes.detail: Refreshing the Right now strip no longer slips back to an older reading a few seconds later, and the age it shows is the age of the figures on screen.

fixes.title: Quick actions stay while you type
fixes.detail: The terminal's quick-actions button stays on screen with the keyboard open and moves with the composer, and the ring opens above the keyboard.

releases.title: Your computer, your terminals, your voice
releases.summary: Open your computer's screen from the phone, work terminals by tab and pane, dictate as you speak, and see plan limits at a glance. This is the first stable release since 0.1.25, so it also includes every change from 0.1.26 to 0.1.28.

features.title: Your computer's screen on your phone
features.detail: Open Computer from any terminal to see and control the desktop. Tap to take control, the pointer follows your finger, a key row and clipboard work both ways, and the phone turns to landscape while you use it. It works over your local network, your private mesh or a direct SSH connection.

features.title: Approve screen sharing once
features.detail: The computer asks for screen-sharing permission once, during setup or pairing, and remembers it, so opening Computer later does not wait on a prompt.

features.title: A screen for servers that have none
features.detail: On a server with no display, muxr starts a private one when you open Computer and keeps other accounts off it.

features.title: Tabs and panes, the way your desk has them
features.detail: The row above the composer lists the workspace's tabs, and + opens a new one that attaches on the first try. The header counts the tab's panes, so you can step between them or split a new one.

features.title: Panes as a live tree
features.detail: Panes shows every tab and agent as a live tree with names, tasks and status, and the pane sheet mirrors the real split on your computer.

features.title: Dictation that writes as you speak
features.detail: Words appear in the composer while you talk, on the terminal and on Home. Pick a language, download a model when you need one, and teach it your own word replacements.

features.title: Right now, at a glance
features.detail: A small strip above Live shows how much of each connected plan is left and when it resets, with the computer's memory, disk and load beside it. Figures stay put through slow or failed reads.

features.title: Agents go by their names
features.detail: Every surface leads with the agent's name and puts its task underneath. Agents can name their own workspace and pane with muxr name.

features.title: Live leads with what needs you
features.detail: Home's Live row shows agents that need you first, then working ones, in a steady order. Finished results stay visible until you open them.

features.title: Seamless agent switching and gestures
features.detail: Swipe between agents in one continuous pager. Gestures in Settings shows what each swipe, pinch and long-press does and lets you change it.

features.title: A rebuilt terminal composer
features.detail: One header, a composer rail and radial quick controls. Edit the key row and add your own keys, send quick replies in one tap, reuse history safely and paste in one tap.

features.title: Answer prompts with a tap
features.detail: When an agent asks a question in the terminal, tap an answer. Other typing is held back while the prompt waits, so a stray key cannot answer it.

features.title: Links you can trust
features.detail: Web links printed in the terminal open safely, and a long-press copies them.

features.title: Shared artifacts, kept
features.detail: Files your agents share gather in one timeline per session. Large files download progressively and resume after a dropped connection, and old history is cleared on a schedule.

features.title: More ways to connect
features.detail: Choose a connection route before pairing, connect over direct SSH, and install your phone's SSH key on the computer from the app. Paired Android phones find the computer again on the local network.

features.title: Install the web app
features.detail: The web app installs as a standalone app, keeps a personal browser paired for 30 days and can receive notifications without an account.

features.title: Guided setup
features.detail: muxr setup walks you through the choices in the terminal and writes them to a config file you or an agent can edit and apply again.

features.title: Home opens instantly
features.detail: Home opens from its last saved state, works offline and reconnects to your computer on its own.

features.title: Near-black dark mode
features.detail: Dark surfaces are now near-black and seamless, with the previous raised look still available in Appearance. Settings show a preview of each choice, and document previews open in your current theme.

features.title: Voice engines explained
features.detail: Settings explains each voice engine and lets you try it, and realtime voice finds and works your agents more reliably.

fixes.title: Faster everywhere
fixes.detail: Cold launch, opening a pane, reconnecting and typing are all quicker, and Android terminal output scrolls smoothly.

fixes.title: Back always goes Home
fixes.detail: Going back from an agent always returns to Home.

fixes.title: A lost connection no longer ends the terminal
fixes.detail: If the computer drops out, the terminal reconnects with a bounded backoff and says what it is doing instead of closing.

fixes.title: Agents started at the desk show up
fixes.detail: Agents you start at the computer appear on Home without restarting anything.

fixes.title: No duplicate alerts
fixes.detail: The agent you are looking at no longer alerts you about itself.

fixes.title: Composer fits short screens
fixes.detail: The composer follows the keyboard, and Home's composer stays usable on short phones.

fixes.title: Voice failures in plain words
fixes.detail: A failed voice call says what went wrong instead of showing a raw error.

fixes.title: Jump to latest works everywhere
fixes.detail: Jump to latest means the same thing in every terminal, and a message sent to a plain shell goes through.

Both desktop packages installed into a clean container with no toolchain and no display, found the prebuilt engine, started it and answered the protocol handshake and a capabilities probe.

releases.title: Steadier terminals, honest usage
releases.summary: Terminal graphics settle sharp instead of flickering, a dropped host reconnects instead of ending your session, and Usage reports only what the transcripts actually show.

features.title: Keyboard on tap is optional
features.detail: Tapping the terminal no longer forces the keyboard open when you only wanted to read. The shortcut is a setting, and it stays hidden on web where it has no meaning.

features.title: Visual release notes
features.detail: Each app version now has one authored release entry that this screen renders directly, and that release preparation turns into an offline HTML report and a Markdown release body.

fixes.title: Terminal images settle sharp
fixes.detail: A pane keeps one resident full image, refines a frame once output goes quiet, re-arms fences it lost, and bounds retained bytes, so scrolling through graphics stops flickering between blurred and sharp frames.

fixes.title: A host outage no longer ends the terminal
fixes.detail: Losing the Herdr connection now recovers the terminal channel instead of closing the session behind it.

fixes.title: Changes and Tools read correctly

fixes.title: Usage counts what the transcripts hold

releases.title: Computers that work together
releases.summary: Authorize paired computers to read, watch, and prompt one another safely.

features.title: Cross-computer agent access
features.detail: Agents list sessions, read output and status, watch completion, and send prompts across allowed computers without shell or destructive access.

features.title: Saved computers in Settings
features.detail: Select paired computers in Settings and see saved computers immediately while live collaboration checks finish.

features.title: Compact public agent guide
features.detail: Load the compact public agent guide with muxr --skill, pull focused topics on demand, and read bounded host history with muxr diagnostics; setup and updates never rewrite agent instructions.

fixes.title: Voice stays on one machine
fixes.detail: Native realtime voice remains pinned to the machine running it while it works with allowed agents elsewhere.

knownLimits: This entry was written after the fact from the shipped release notes; no verification record was retained for it.

legacyEntries.title: Pairing that stays paired
legacyEntries.summary: QRs scan reliably, saved machines switch cleanly, and browser access survives refresh.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Scan a four-margin terminal QR directly from Settings → Pair another machine, with manual entry beside it.
- See the active computer on Home and switch saved machines there; stale sessions and forgotten computers disappear immediately.
- Show the host's real platform and only launchable agents in the Home composer.
- Pair browsers from one short two-minute HTTPS link with host-enforced control or explicit view-only access.
- Wait for browser storage to commit before setup reports success, recover interrupted grant indexes, and show an explicit recovery screen instead of silently appearing unpaired.

legacyEntries.title: One tap, one destination
legacyEntries.summary: Pairing, Usage, machine details, and Preview lose their duplicate steps.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Keep Scan QR and manual pairing separate; the manual screen now contains only the string field and Connect.
- Open the provider-tab Usage screen from one plain pill beside Machine.
- See the active transport, relay URL, and muxr CLI version in machine details.
- Preview only detected HTML frontends by page title and carry the paired relay through the tunnel.

legacyEntries.title: Pair without the payload
legacyEntries.summary: A short relay-qualified code replaces the giant native pairing string.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Enter one short two-minute pairing string or scan the same value as a QR.
- Pair through LAN, Tailscale, Cloudflare, or a custom relay without a central discovery service.
- Pairing lookups are encrypted, single-use, and deleted after resolution; completed handoffs are deleted after grant delivery.

legacyEntries.title: Polish everywhere
legacyEntries.summary: A design-review pass plus simpler, fewer bundled plugins.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Proper green/red diffs, theme-correct voice overlay, and press feedback across terminal, sheets, and plugin screens.
- Copy a link from recent terminal output in one tap from the Actions menu.
- Fewer, simpler bundled plugins: Code (files, changes, and history) and Status (usage and vitals).
- The read-only browser now shows audited read-only plugin screens like Usage and Files; bundled plugin permissions refresh once after this safety upgrade.
- The setup menu guides instead of dead-ending, pairing recovers from expired sessions, and the app names OMP correctly.

legacyEntries.title: Visual usage and steadier voice
legacyEntries.summary: Charts and progress in plugin screens, plus screen-off voice fixes.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- See today’s per-agent token activity as charts and Codex limits as progress rings on a native Usage screen.
- Build richer plugin screens with data-bound progress, responsive columns, and bounded bar/ring charts — the same public UI vocabulary every extension uses.
- Keep voice alive with the screen off: wake and Wi-Fi locks during calls, speaking counts as activity, and reconnects recover over long sessions.
- Plugin failures show one clean message instead of technical detail; Git history shows a friendly empty state when a session has no folder.

legacyEntries.title: Readable code and honest usage
legacyEntries.summary: Syntax-highlighted source and offline multi-agent activity.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Read source with line numbers and consistent syntax highlighting across Files, Markdown, plugin screens, and diffs.
- Use the same bounded code and diff views from third-party plugins without HTML or native modules.
- See today’s local coding-agent activity through a pinned offline ccusage backend, alongside current Codex limits.
- Keep costs, prompts, model names, projects, and session details out of the Usage card.

legacyEntries.title: Shared relays and safer setup
legacyEntries.summary: Guided onboarding, machine-scoped VPS relays, and runtime agent discovery.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Run `muxr` for a reviewed, Cancel-first setup and maintenance menu.
- Host one encrypted relay for several machines without copying relay-owner authority.
- Pair a read-only browser from a clickable HTTPS link with clear eight-hour expiry and recovery.
- Choose agents from the connected Herdr host and view safe coding-CLI usage status.

legacyEntries.title: muxr
legacyEntries.summary: A focused mobile control surface for coding agents running through Herdr.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Watch sessions, terminals, changes, and attention state from your phone.
- Send keys, inspect attachments, and start agents in a selected workspace.
- Use provider-neutral realtime voice or fully local Whisper dictation.
